result:
All 617 tests pass and typecheck is clean. The fix is complete.

Root cause: `organizationSettingsSchema` defined every field with `.default(...)`. Both `updateOrganizationSchema` (action-level validation) and `organization-service.ts`'s re-validation used `.partial()` on that schema, but in this Zod version, `.optional()`/`.partial()` wrapping a field that already has `.default()` still applies the default when the field is omitted — it doesn't leave it `undefined`. So any partial settings update (e.g. only submitting `allowPublicProjects`/`requireTwoFactor`/`digestHourUtc` from the general settings form) got expanded into a fully-populated object with defaults standing in for the omitted fields (`defaultIssueStatus: "backlog"`, `enabledFlagOverrides: []`), which then clobbered the stored values when merged in the repository.

Fix: split the schema into `organizationSettingsShape` (bare field types, no defaults) and:
- `organizationSettingsSchema` — the shape with `.default(...)` applied, for full/authoritative values.
- `organizationSettingsPatchSchema` — `z.object(organizationSettingsShape).partial()`, which has no defaults to fall back to, so omitted fields are genuinely absent (verified via a quick node probe) while explicit `false`/`0`/`[]` still pass through correctly.

Both `updateOrganizationSchema.settings` and the re-validation in `updateOrganization()` (`src/server/services/organization-service.ts`) now use `organizationSettingsPatchSchema`, so a save only ever changes the fields actually submitted, and other workspaces/fields are untouched.
